key_insight: PhysAssistBench shows that medical LLMs still struggle to coordinate clinical knowledge, patient communication, and EHR tool use in one realistic doctor-assist workflow.
clinical_relevance: This matters because near-term clinical AI is more likely to support physicians in interactive tasks than to replace them, and reliability in those workflows is still limited.
method: Built PhysAssistBench from real MIMIC-IV cases.
Used a scalable pipeline to create interactive, record-grounded agentic patients.
Curated a bilingual benchmark with physician-validated multi-turn scenarios.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 1,296 manually reviewed and physician-validated turns, and experiments found leading LLMs remain unreliable in this interactive setting.
watch_item: The benchmark is promising, but translating performance into safe bedside use will still require careful validation across communication, reasoning, and EHR interaction.
paper_title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance
